title: groundstation field test №16: the cards stops 21 to 27 set out to fix, re-run on 0.47.0
heading: THE FIELD TEST №16
sub: groundstation · 7 prompts re-run · 7 live artifacts · 5 fixed, 2 partly, 0 the same · October 26, 2026 · Development Seed labs
lede: The 7 cards from field test 15 that stops 21 to 27 were charted to fix, asked again in the same words on main at 0.47.0 (PRs 83 to 89, all landed the same day). Each learning opens with its verdict, grounded only in the new output: 5 fixed, 2 partly, 0 the same. One card found a break that is not groundstation's: Planetary Computer's mosaic register now answers with a different key, so WorldCover maps die on 0.47.0 as shipped.

stats.label: cards re-asked on 0.47.0, one per stop from 21 to 27
fixed · partly · the same, each verdict grounded in the new output
live artifacts: maps, a postcard, a 3D view, swipes, a timelapse; plus 3 phone and desktop screenshots
new findings: a Planetary Computer register key change, scaling factors missing from the compare result, the credit inside the attribution bar at 390 px, a water-index mean that is not an area

cases.answer: Rolling Fork gives the same NDVI as field test 15, 0.198 before and 0.2274 after (delta 0.0294), and this time the 46% cloud on the before scene is named by scene id. The data behind the picture is Sentinel-2 L2A tile 15SXS, S2A_15SXS_20230219_0_L2A before (cloud 45.558468) and S2B_15SXS_20230326_0_L2A after (cloud 0.767861, 2 days after the tornado). Scaling was on by default and the means did not move, because a normalized difference is a ratio and Earth Search already has the -0.1 offset in its pixels. The adjuster's 2 notes are on the page 2 times each. An NDVI mean over the whole box still says nothing about the damage track.
cases.artifact_label: swipe: Rolling Fork NDVI with the adjuster's notes ↗
cases.learning: Partly. Field test 15 said the result "also says the means are raw digital numbers with the offset not applied", and stop 23 promised compare_dates would return values "with scaling_applied true and the factors named". Field test 15 also said "Now notes reaches the page (2 matches per string) and the bogus adjuster key is returned as stack_facts_ignored". Now the notes still match 2 times per string, adjuster still comes back named, the caveat names scene S2A_15SXS_20230219_0_L2A at 46% against a 20% threshold, and the caller-passed geocoded: "nominatim" for a hand-picked box comes back in stack_facts_ignored beside adjuster. The raw scaling_note is gone from the default run and scaling_applied is true. The out_path outside the repo now returns an error dict of its own, where field test 15's flood card got an uncaught KeyError: 'map_path'; here there is no KeyError and no file was written. Why Partly: this is stop 23 half done, not a new break. Scaling is applied, but the factors are not named in the default compare_dates result, which only says scaling_applied: true; the scale 0.0001 and the offset story appear in the apply_scaling=False scaling_note and in compute_statistics band_scaling (which I ran once on the after scene), not in the default compare_dates answer. The raw note says "the declared offset -0.1 is already in the pixels", which is why the means could not move. The raw and scaled means are identical to 4 places, so for this index the correction changes nothing a reader could see, which means this card cannot show scaling working on a number. Not checked: whether the Stack panel on the page still credits Nominatim after geocoded was ignored, a scaled non-ratio expression, and any other place.
cases.shows: stop 23 scaling_applied and raw run beside it · stop 21 cloud caveat names the scene id · geocoded in stack_facts_ignored · adjuster still named · notes 2 matches each · out_path outside the repo returns an error dict

cases.answer: With no rescale given, render_map worked out its own stretch, 13682 to 14788 for both tiles, and the Valley reads clearly with no hand range. Both layers in state.layers carry rescale_used: 13682,14788 with the basis "2nd to 98th percentile of the raw values over the box, widest of 2 scenes", so the two tiles share one range. Valley floor is light yellow to orange, the foothills orange to purple, the high Sierra black. The white patches in the Valley and the south are pixels flagged not produced, most of them cloud: in h08v05 every nodata pixel in the box (57280 of 216568) is flagged not produced, 33482 of them as cloud (QC 2), and the cloud share climbs from 4% at -120.50 to -120.12 to 49% at -118.98 to -118.60. The other 23798 are QC 3 along the west edge. The east-edge stripe I could not pin down: it lies east of the box, row reads show cloud runs with valid pixels on both sides so it is not a tile edge, but I did not match it pixel for pixel.

cases.learning: Fixed. Field test 15 said: "the stretch I first copied from field test 14's tile_url_template call (14500 to 16000; field test 14 drew no map) drew nearly all the land black in late October, so I re-rendered with 13500 to 15500". This round no range was passed, and the map came back with a stretch from the data, 13682 to 14788, its basis named, one range for both tiles. The picture is legible at 1000 by 700 and a little hotter in colour than field test 15's hand range, because the data range is narrower (the Valley floor sits near the top of the ramp). Field test 15 also noticed white patches and a white east stripe that no reviewer had opened. The patches are pixels that QC_Day marks as not produced: in h08v05, 33482 for cloud (QC 2) and 23798 for other reasons (QC 3) toward the west edge, on a scene the search already gave as 28% cloud. The stripe is still there in the still and I could not say what it is. Stumbles that remain: the result has no top-level rescale_used, it sits in each layer under state.layers; the recommended h08v05 scene is still the 28% cloud one, and the cloud holes are in the Valley's south and east where a public health reader would look. Not checked: whether a caller-given rescale is used as given, whether a categorical colormap is left alone, other dates, and how many Valley pixels exceed 14788 and clip to the top colour.

cases.answer: The page does most of what stop 25 promised at 390 px, but the call that builds it fails today with KeyError 'id', so a user would not get this map at all. The call fails inside _pc_mosaic_id because Planetary Computer's register endpoint now returns searchid for esa-worldcover and the code reads id; I built the page with a patch in my own script and left the repo alone. On that page the layers panel is folded at 390 px (a 240 by 113.1 box) and opens on a tap to 240 by 446.1. Each layer reads "2021-01-01" with its tile id under it, six rows, no longer the 40% of the screen that field test 15 saw at rest. STACK sits to the right of the title, 16.8 px clear of the panel and 32.8 px clear of the title text. New look: at 390 px the Development Seed credit (top 803, bottom 820) sits inside the attribution bar (top 790, bottom 834) and covers its second line. At 1280 px the two do not touch.

cases.learning: Partly. Field test 15 said: "the 6 layer checkboxes are now named by tile ... so the layer panel fills the top 40% of the screen and covers the north of the lake, and the STACK button still sits on its title." On the page now, the panel is folded at load at 390 px and opens on a tap (details.fold false, then true), STACK is clear of the title, and the layer list and tool result keep the tile id beside a shared name. Two things do not match the promise or the old picture. The layer name is the date alone, "2021-01-01", not the collection plus date that stop 25 promised: with no name passed, a coverage_set layer falls back to its date, and stop 25's own check passed the name "WorldCover 2021" by hand. Field test 15's call passed no name either. That part is the old thing not fully fixed. The other is a new break, not stop 25 unfixed: the call itself fails as shipped with KeyError 'id' from the mosaic register answer, so the page on this card came from a call patched in my own script, not from 0.47.0 as shipped. It breaks this card's prompt today, and it looks like the same trap field test 8 guarded for slow registrations, only for a changed reply and not a slow one. Opened, the panel is 446.1 px tall of 844 and covers the north of the lake until closed, by choice now. Course candidates: read searchid or fall back to item tiles when id is absent; the Development Seed credit overlapping the attribution bar at 390 px (measured from the DOM). Not checked: other phone widths, a name passed in the layer, whether the failure hits other collections, and the page on a real phone.

cases.answer: A bare "Portland" now lists 4 candidates, all named Portland, with the state in the note, and the Casco Bay recommendation is a scene that covers 100.0% of the box, so the card has no wedge to print. The refusal names Oregon (an urban centre and a locality) and Maine (a locality and an urban centre) and the Guadeloupe row is gone. For Casco Bay the recommended scene is LC09_L2SP_012030_20261005_02_T1 (15.28% cloud), chosen because it covers 100.0% while the clearest scene (0.33% cloud) covers 84.2%. Only 0.0405 of its pixels are near-black, against 0.3372 in field test 15. The newest 100% scene is the 2026-10-21 one at 23.01% cloud, and the pick is 16 days older than it. The output does not say why that newer scene lost: the reason string only compares the pick with the clearest scene. Rendering the old 66.6% scene on purpose shows the other branch: its card caption now reads "31.6% of the box uncovered, mostly south", with coverage_pct 68.4 in the result.
cases.learning: Fixed. Field test 15 said of the candidate list: "the Guadeloupe candidate is named 'Le Moule (GP, locality)', not Portland", and of the card: "a search of the card HTML for uncovered, no-data and no data finds 0 matches", with uncovered_pct 31.6, south, and 33.7% near-black pixels. Now the list holds only Portlands and the note spells the states out (Oregon, Maine) instead of coordinates. The recommendation goes through coverage first (100.0% over 84.2%). The wedge now reaches the card: the old scene's caption carries 31.6% uncovered, mostly south, so a reader of the card alone gets a warning; the figures 31.6 and 0.3372 match field test 15 to the digit. Stumbles that remain: the card prints only a caption phrase, not the words no-data (0 matches) and not the coverage figure 68.4, and when coverage is 100.0 it prints nothing about coverage at all (0 matches for uncovered and for 100.0); the pick is not the newest 100% scene, it is the lower-cloud one 16 days earlier, so a pilot asking for the latest pass gets an older one, and nothing in the output says why. Read from the code, not the output: the recommendation keeps scenes within 5 points of the least cloud among the full-coverage ones before it applies the 7-day recency band, so the 23.01% scene drops out at the cloud step (more than 5 points above 15.28) and never reaches the band; the black wedge itself is not filled, and the tool's own note says that needs direct COG access, which planetary-computer does not offer. Not checked: the card by eye, and the geocoded Portland, Maine box against the casco box (they differ; I used casco as field test 15 did).
